question: Nursing is best described as a combination of which two disciplines?

options.A: Anatomy and history
options.B: Research and finance
options.C: Art and science
options.D: Theory and politics

explanation: Nursing combines the compassionate human touch of an art with the evidence-based rigor of a science. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h1)

question: A nurse focuses primarily on diagnosing and treating what aspect of a patient's condition?

options.A: Human responses
options.B: Financial status
options.C: Surgical pathology
options.D: Cellular pathology

explanation: While doctors diagnose the medical disease, nurses diagnose and treat human responses to health issues and life processes. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h1)

question: Who is widely recognized as the founder of modern professional nursing?

options.A: Clara Barton
options.B: Florence Nightingale
options.C: Mary Seacole
options.D: Virginia Henderson

explanation: Florence Nightingale transformed nursing during the Crimean War by emphasizing sanitation, organization, and formal training. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h2)

question: The historical shift of nursing into academic settings primarily aimed to achieve what goal?

options.A: Establish research-backed clinical guidelines
options.B: Reduce the working hours of doctors
options.C: Increase hospital revenue generation
options.D: Limit the responsibilities of ward staff

explanation: Moving nursing into universities and colleges helped build a strong scientific foundation for clinical practice. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h2)

question: The International Council of Nurses states that nursing care can be provided to whom?

options.A: Both sick and well individuals
options.B: Individuals with chronic illness exclusively
options.C: Patients admitted to surgery only
options.D: Only critically ill patients

explanation: Nursing spans health promotion and illness prevention for healthy populations as well as care for the sick. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h3)

question: According to major global organizations, nursing practice requires which operational approach?

options.A: Direct supervision by hospital owners
options.B: Autonomous and collaborative care
options.C: Purely administrative oversight
options.D: Strictly independent decision-making

explanation: Nurses must be capable of independent clinical judgment while working closely with other members of the healthcare team. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which component of the nursing metaparadigm refers to internal and external surroundings?

options.A: Environment
options.B: Health
options.C: Person
options.D: Nursing

explanation: Environment encompasses all physical, social, and cultural conditions affecting the patient. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h4)

question: How is 'health' viewed within the nursing metaparadigm?

options.A: The total absence of any biological disease
options.B: A permanent condition achieved at discharge
options.C: A fixed score on a laboratory test
options.D: A dynamic and subjective state of well-being

explanation: Health is not merely the absence of disease; it changes continuously and is experienced uniquely by each individual. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h4)

question: A nurse who explains a prescribed medication procedure to an anxious patient is primarily acting as an?

options.A: Administrator
options.B: Educator
options.C: Auditor
options.D: Pharmacist

explanation: Teaching patients about their health conditions and treatments is a core educational role of the nurse. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h5)

question: Professional accountability in nursing requires a practitioner to do what?

options.A: Avoid making independent decisions
options.B: Delegate all complex tasks to junior staff
options.C: Accept responsibility for their clinical actions
options.D: Blame hospital management for poor supplies

explanation: Accountability means nurses own the outcomes of their nursing care and maintain high standards of practice. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which body legally regulates nursing education and practice in Nigeria?

options.A: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.B: West African Health Organization
options.C: Nigerian Medical Association
options.D: Federal Ministry of Education

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body charged with regulating nursing standards, training, and licensure in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why is a clearly defined scope of nursing practice important in healthcare settings?

options.A: It ensures nurses receive higher salaries than doctors
options.B: It protects the public from unqualified practitioners
options.C: It eliminates the need for patient documentation
options.D: It prevents nurses from working in rural areas

explanation: Defining the legal boundaries of practice ensures safe care and prevents unqualified individuals from harming patients. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h6)

question: Ancient Greek physician Hippocrates transformed medicine by suggesting what origin for diseases?

options.A: Evil spirits
options.B: Demonic possession
options.C: Natural causes
options.D: Divine wrath

explanation: Hippocrates argued that illnesses arose from physical and environmental factors rather than supernatural punishment. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h1)

question: Early nursing and healing practices in ancient societies were primarily managed by which group?

options.A: Priests and shamans
options.B: Government health inspectors
options.C: Certified military nurses
options.D: Trained university doctors

explanation: Because disease was viewed through a spiritual lens, religious leaders and medicine men typically directed early healing rituals. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which military-monastic group established large hospitals and structured care during the Crusades?

options.A: Roman Legion medics
options.B: Red Cross Society
options.C: Nightingale Brigade
options.D: Knights Hospitaller

explanation: The Knights Hospitaller built extensive medical facilities to care for pilgrims and wounded soldiers during the Crusades. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h2)

question: Religious influence primarily framed early nursing care as which of the following?

options.A: A high-paying corporate profession
options.B: A strictly political movement
options.C: A moral and charitable vocation
options.D: A secular scientific experiment

explanation: Religious institutions viewed caring for the sick as an act of divine service and moral duty. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h2)

question: Florence Nightingale first gained widespread prominence during which armed conflict?

options.A: World War I
options.B: Crimean War
options.C: Nigerian Civil War
options.D: American Civil War

explanation: Nightingale led a team of nurses to Scutari during the Crimean War, significantly lowering death rates through sanitation. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h3)

question: What core principle defined the Nightingale model of nursing education?

options.A: Training should happen entirely through medical textbooks
options.B: Students should focus only on spiritual counseling
options.C: Hospitals should control all nursing curriculum finances
options.D: Schools must be independent and led by nurses

explanation: Nightingale insisted that nursing training institutions maintain autonomy from hospital administration and be directed by experienced nurses. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h3)

question: Who introduced Western-style formal nursing training to Nigeria during the colonial era?

options.A: The World Health Organization
options.B: United Nations volunteers
options.C: Local traditional rulers
options.D: Christian missionaries

explanation: Christian mission societies built early hospitals and started the first formal training programs for local nurses. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h4)

question: The primary body responsible for regulating nursing standards and training in Nigeria is the:

options.A: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.B: West African Health Community
options.C: Nigerian Medical Association
options.D: Federal Ministry of Education

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria regulates professional practice, examinations, and school accreditations nationwide. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why were nursing registration acts and licensure systems originally established?

options.A: To protect the public from unqualified practitioners
options.B: To increase government tax revenue from clinics
options.C: To limit the total number of working hospitals
options.D: To eliminate the need for clinical examinations

explanation: Licensure laws ensure that only individuals who meet verified competency standards are permitted to practice nursing. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h5)

question: The transition of nursing education from hospital-based apprenticeships to universities signifies what change?

options.A: Complete elimination of practical hospital bedside training
options.B: Elevation of nursing to a recognized academic and scientific profession
options.C: Shift of regulatory control away from professional councils
options.D: Reduction in the total scope of nursing responsibilities

explanation: Moving education into higher institutions anchors nursing practice in formal research, critical thinking, and advanced sciences. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h5)

question: Electronic health records and telemedicine are examples of what driving force in modern nursing?

options.A: Traditional herbal medicine
options.B: Technological integration
options.C: Colonial health policy
options.D: Monastic care routines

explanation: Digital tools and communication technologies are central components of contemporary healthcare transformation. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is a major result of expanding advanced practice nursing roles in modern healthcare systems?

options.A: Lower educational requirements for hospital supervisors
options.B: Complete restriction from performing physical assessments
options.C: Greater autonomy in patient diagnosis and treatment
options.D: Total replacement of physicians in surgical theatres

explanation: Advanced practice nurses take on expanded clinical duties, including diagnosing conditions and prescribing treatments in many settings. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is the official World Health Organization definition of health?

options.A: A balance between spiritual and physical energies
options.B: An individual's ability to perform daily work duties
options.C: The total absence of any diagnosed physical disease
options.D: A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being

explanation: The WHO definition looks beyond simple physical pathology to include social and mental dimensions. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h1)

question: How does illness differ fundamentally from disease in clinical practice?

options.A: Illness affects the mind only, while disease affects the physical body
options.B: Disease requires hospitalization, whereas illness can be treated at home
options.C: Illness is a subjective feeling, while disease is a pathological process
options.D: Disease is temporary, but illness is always a chronic condition

explanation: A person can have a disease like hypertension without feeling ill, just as someone can feel ill without a clear medical disease. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which health model defines wellness by a person's ability to fulfill daily societal roles?

options.A: Clinical Model
options.B: Role Performance Model
options.C: Adaptive Model
options.D: Eudaimonistic Model

explanation: This model considers a person healthy as long as they can successfully go to work, school, or manage family duties. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h2)

question: A patient considers themselves healthy only when they have zero physical pain. Which model applies here?

options.A: Adaptive Model
options.B: Eudaimonistic Model
options.C: Clinical Model
options.D: Role Performance Model

explanation: The clinical model strictly equates health with the complete absence of disease symptoms. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h2)

question: What are the two extreme poles of the illness-wellness continuum?

options.A: Complete bedrest and active rehabilitation
options.B: Physical health and mental stability
options.C: Premature death and high-level wellness
options.D: Acute infection and chronic disability

explanation: The continuum spans from the lowest possible state of health to the highest possible state of vitality. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of using the illness-wellness continuum in nursing assessment?

options.A: To accurately predict the exact date a patient will be discharged
options.B: To view health as a dynamic, changing process rather than a fixed state
options.C: To determine the financial cost of chronic disease management
options.D: To categorize patients strictly into healthy or diseased groups

explanation: The continuum helps clinicians see that individuals are constantly moving between different levels of health and illness. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h3)

question: Which dimension of health involves the ability to form healthy relationships with others?

options.A: Physical dimension
options.B: Spiritual dimension
options.C: Mental dimension
options.D: Social dimension

explanation: The social dimension centers on interaction, communication, and connection within communities and families. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h4)

question: A patient draws strength from personal faith and a deep sense of life purpose during a crisis. Which dimension is highlighted?

options.A: Environmental dimension
options.B: Spiritual dimension
options.C: Social dimension
options.D: Emotional dimension

explanation: Spirituality involves finding meaning, purpose, and inner peace, often supported by religious or personal belief systems. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h4)

question: At which stage of illness behavior does a person usually seek validation from family members?

options.A: Recovery and rehabilitation
options.B: Experiencing symptoms
options.C: Assuming the sick role
options.D: Assuming the dependent role

explanation: In the sick role stage, individuals look for confirmation from others that they are indeed unwell and excused from routine duties. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h5)

question: A hospitalized patient hands over all personal decision-making regarding daily care to the nurses and doctors. Which stage does this reflect?

options.A: Experiencing symptoms
options.B: Seeking medical care
options.C: Assuming the sick role
options.D: Assuming the dependent role

explanation: The dependent role involves relinquishing personal control and accepting help from professional caregivers. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which of the following is an internal variable that affects a person's health?

options.A: Housing conditions
options.B: Socioeconomic status
options.C: Healthcare access
options.D: Genetic makeup

explanation: Genetics, age, and sex are internal biological characteristics that influence susceptibility to various diseases. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why must nurses consider a patient's cultural background when planning care?

options.A: Culture determines the exact financial cost of prescribed medications
options.B: Government regulations require cultural documentation for hospital discharge
options.C: Culture shapes beliefs about what causes illness and how to seek treatment
options.D: Cultural beliefs replace the need for standard diagnostic laboratory tests

explanation: Cultural values strongly influence health practices, medication compliance, and overall healing expectations. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h6)

question: How does a chronic illness in a parent typically affect family dynamics?

options.A: Financial stability automatically improves due to government subsidies
options.B: The family unit usually becomes completely isolated from the community
options.C: Children lose all interest in school and academic performance
options.D: Other family members must take on new roles and increased responsibilities

explanation: Chronic illness causes a redistribution of chores and duties among available family members. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h7)

question: What psychological response is a patient most likely to experience following a major organ surgery?

options.A: Heightened physical stamina
options.B: Permanent memory loss
options.C: Complete emotional apathy
options.D: Altered body image

explanation: Surgical procedures, scars, and organ loss often lead to significant changes in how patients view their physical bodies. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h7)

question: What are basic human needs considered to be in clinical practice?

options.A: Elements required for human survival and health
options.B: Optional comforts provided only in private hospitals
options.C: Surgical interventions required after major trauma
options.D: Administrative rules set by hospital management boards

explanation: Basic human needs represent the essential physiological and psychological requirements that every individual needs to maintain life and well-being. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why must nurses look beyond a disease diagnosis when assessing a patient?

options.A: Patients prefer discussing their family problems instead of medical treatments
options.B: Doctors only focus on medication while nurses handle cleaning duties
options.C: Hospital insurance policies require personal life history documentation
options.D: Illness and hospitalization often compromise a patient's ability to meet basic needs

explanation: Disease and admission disrupt normal routines, making it difficult for patients to independently fulfill their fundamental daily requirements. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which need sits at the very base of Maslow's pyramid?

options.A: Safety needs
options.B: Belonging needs
options.C: Self-esteem needs
options.D: Physiological needs

explanation: Physiological requirements form the foundation of Maslow's hierarchy because they are essential for immediate biological survival. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is true about the movement between levels in Maslow's hierarchy?

options.A: Psychological needs always take strict priority over physical emergencies
options.B: A person must completely fulfill self-actualization before eating or drinking
options.C: Individuals progress through every level in an identical, unchangeable timeframe
options.D: Lower needs must be met to some degree before higher needs are pursued

explanation: The hierarchy is flexible rather than rigid, allowing individuals to address higher goals while lower needs are only partially satisfied. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which physiological need requires the most immediate nursing intervention during an emergency?

options.A: Nutrition
options.B: Oxygenation
options.C: Elimination
options.D: Self-esteem

explanation: Oxygen is the most critical physiological requirement because brain cells begin to die within minutes if deprived of oxygen supply. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h3)

question: A newly admitted patient shows signs of severe dehydration and dry mucous membranes. Which nursing action addresses this physiological deficit?

options.A: Tracking fluid intake and output closely
options.B: Assessing the patient for signs of depression
options.C: Encouraging participation in ward social activities
options.D: Teaching the patient about personal achievement goals

explanation: Monitoring fluid balance directly targets the physiological need for hydration and helps guide rehydration therapy. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is a primary nursing action to ensure physical safety in the ward?

options.A: Providing gourmet meals suited to cultural preferences
options.B: Verifying patient identification before giving medications
options.C: Ensuring the patient achieves personal life ambitions
options.D: Organizing group recreational therapy sessions daily

explanation: Checking patient identity prevents medication errors and directly protects the patient from physical harm. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why do hospitalized patients frequently experience threats to their safety needs?

options.A: The healthcare environment is unfamiliar and exposes them to procedural risks
options.B: Medical insurance covers all expenses without any administrative delay
options.C: Hospitals forbid patients from eating traditional local foods
options.D: Ward nurses rarely check vital signs during night shifts

explanation: Strange surroundings, loss of independence, and invasive procedures make patients feel vulnerable and insecure. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which factor heavily supports love and belonging needs for patients in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Involving extended family members in the care process
options.B: Isolating the patient completely from external visitors
options.C: Strictly limiting conversations to clinical medical updates
options.D: Focusing solely on intravenous drug administration schedules

explanation: Extended family networks provide vital emotional and social support that reinforces the patient's sense of belonging and community. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h5)

question: How does severe social isolation negatively impact a hospitalized patient?

options.A: It can cause despair and slow down physical recovery
options.B: It eliminates the risk of nosocomial infections
options.C: It automatically improves surgical wound healing times
options.D: It increases independent physiological organ functioning

explanation: Lack of social connection and emotional support contributes to psychological distress, which negatively affects overall physical healing. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to support a patient's self-esteem during recovery?

options.A: Making all clinical decisions without consulting the patient
options.B: Encouraging maximum possible independence in daily self-care activities
options.C: Restricting family visits to maintain strict hospital quietness
options.D: Telling the patient to ignore physical changes caused by illness

explanation: Allowing patients to do what they can for themselves fosters a sense of competence, dignity, and personal control. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which of the following describes the need for self-actualization?

options.A: Securing adequate clean drinking water and food supplies
options.B: Reaching one's maximum potential and personal growth
options.C: Maintaining stable blood pressure and normal body temperature
options.D: Gaining respect and recognition from medical colleagues

explanation: Self-actualization represents the apex of human development where an individual seeks fulfillment and realizes their personal capabilities. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why must nurses consider culture and religion when addressing basic human needs?

options.A: Religious practices replace the need for physical surgical interventions
options.B: Hospital regulations require patients to abandon traditional practices
options.C: Cultural background determines the exact dosage of prescribed antibiotics
options.D: Belief systems influence dietary habits, pain expression, and views on care

explanation: Cultural and religious beliefs heavily shape how individuals perceive health, illness, and acceptable forms of healthcare delivery. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h7)

question: Which factor directly affects a person's baseline health based on their living conditions and income?

options.A: Standard hospital visiting hours
options.B: Lifestyle and socioeconomic status
options.C: The number of nurses on duty
options.D: The specific brand of hospital bed

explanation: Socioeconomic status determines access to vital resources like proper nutrition, clean water, and safe housing, which influence overall health. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h7)

question: During which phase of the nursing process are patient goals prioritized using Maslow's hierarchy?

options.A: Assessment
options.B: Evaluation
options.C: Implementation
options.D: Planning

explanation: The planning stage involves setting goals and prioritizing patient care interventions based on the urgency of unmet basic needs. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h8)

question: A nurse reviews a patient's care plan after three days of treatment to see if the targeted health outcomes were achieved. What phase of the nursing process is this?

options.A: Assessment
options.B: Implementation
options.C: Diagnosis
options.D: Evaluation

explanation: Evaluation involves checking patient progress against expected outcomes to determine if nursing interventions were effective. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of a professional nursing organization?

options.A: To supply medical drugs to clinics
options.B: To train doctors in emergency care
options.C: To advance nursing practice and protect practitioners
options.D: To run private hospitals for profit

explanation: Professional nursing bodies exist to support practitioners, set standards, and advance the profession as a whole. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T5#GNS112_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why is unity among nurses through professional bodies important in healthcare systems?

options.A: It prevents doctors from making clinical diagnoses
options.B: It ensures all nurses receive equal salaries nationwide
options.C: It eliminates the need for hospital management teams
options.D: It gives nurses a stronger voice in policy decisions

explanation: A collective body allows nurses to advocate effectively for better working conditions and health policies. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T5#GNS112_U1_T5_h1)

question: A key benefit of joining a nursing professional association is gaining access to what resource?

options.A: Free housing accommodations in the city
options.B: Exemption from hospital shift duties
options.C: Automatic promotions to senior medical ranks
options.D: Updated clinical guidelines and research journals

explanation: Professional associations regularly publish materials that keep members informed about current evidence-based practices. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T5#GNS112_U1_T5_h2)

question: How does professional networking within an nursing organization help a young clinician?

options.A: It removes the requirement for annual license renewal
options.B: It allows them to open a pharmacy without a permit
options.C: It guarantees them a scholarship abroad
options.D: It connects them with experienced mentors for career guidance

explanation: Networking opens doors to mentorship, professional support, and career advancement opportunities. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T5#GNS112_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary focus of the International Council of Nurses (ICN)?

options.A: Providing direct patient care in disaster zones
options.B: Uniting nursing associations globally and setting international standards
options.C: Licensing individual nurses to practice in rural Nigerian clinics
options.D: Setting the specific salary scale for state hospitals

explanation: The ICN is a federation of national nurses associations working to represent nurses worldwide. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T5#GNS112_U1_T5_h3)

question: A major difference between national and international nursing bodies is that national bodies focus on...

options.A: Country-specific labor rights and local healthcare challenges
options.B: Writing textbooks for every nursing school worldwide
options.C: Issuing international passports to travelling clinicians
options.D: Global pandemics without considering local laws

explanation: National organizations deal directly with the unique industrial and professional needs within their specific country. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T5#GNS112_U1_T5_h3)

question: What do professional organizations draft to guide the moral conduct of nurses?

options.A: Pharmaceutical pricing lists
options.B: Hospital architectural blueprints
options.C: Codes of ethics
options.D: Medical insurance policies

explanation: Codes of ethics provide the foundational moral rules and duties expected of every practicing nurse. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T5#GNS112_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why do professional bodies actively lobby government agencies regarding nurse-to-patient ratios?

options.A: To prevent staff burnout and protect patient safety
options.B: To increase the cost of nursing school tuition fees
options.C: To reduce the number of working hours for doctors
options.D: To ensure hospitals purchase expensive foreign equipment

explanation: Proper staffing ratios are vital for reducing medical errors and maintaining high standards of patient care. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T5#GNS112_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is a major reason professional organizations provide continuing education programs?

options.A: To test students before they enter clinical wards
options.B: To help nurses keep up with medical and technological changes
options.C: To replace traditional nursing school diploma programs
options.D: To generate revenue to build private commercial businesses

explanation: Continuing education ensures that practicing clinicians stay updated on modern healthcare practices. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T5#GNS112_U1_T5_h5)

question: How does continuing professional development directly affect a nurse's practicing license in Nigeria?

options.A: It grants automatic promotion to the director of nursing
options.B: It exempts the nurse from paying professional dues
options.C: It allows the nurse to retire early with a full pension
options.D: Credits earned are often required for annual license renewal

explanation: Regulatory councils frequently tie license renewal to the completion of verified professional development units. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T5#GNS112_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the main goal of public health agencies compared to individual hospital care?

options.A: Surgical intervention for chronic illnesses
options.B: Population-wide disease prevention and health promotion
options.C: Individual patient bedside nursing care
options.D: Private hospital revenue generation

explanation: Health maintenance agencies focus on community health, disease tracking, and prevention rather than treating single patients at the bedside. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T6#GNS112_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why do clinical nurses need to understand the role of health maintenance agencies?

options.A: To manage the financial budget of government hospitals
options.B: To participate effectively in public health campaigns and disease reporting
options.C: To handle international travel arrangements for patients
options.D: To prescribe medications outside their normal scope of practice

explanation: Nurses collaborate with these agencies during outbreaks, immunizations, and mandatory reporting procedures. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T6#GNS112_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which Nigerian agency is responsible for regulating food and pharmaceutical drugs?

options.A: Nigerian Medical Association
options.B: NPHCDA
options.C: NAFDAC
options.D: Federal Ministry of Health

explanation: NAFDAC is specifically mandated to regulate and control the manufacture, importation, and use of drugs, food, and medical devices in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T6#GNS112_U1_T6_h2)

question: A nurse finds a batch of expired vaccines at a primary health clinic. Which national body handles immunization programs to address this?

options.A: Standard Organisation of Nigeria
options.B: NPHCDA
options.C: Ministry of Education
options.D: Federal Road Safety Corps

explanation: The National Primary Health Care Development Agency oversees immunization programs and primary health facility operations in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T6#GNS112_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is the main global health role of the World Health Organization (WHO)?

options.A: Coordinating international health standards and disease surveillance
options.B: Funding local university nursing scholarships
options.C: Enforcing local food safety laws in Nigeria
options.D: Building private hospitals in developing countries

explanation: The WHO acts as the lead international authority for establishing health guidelines and monitoring global disease outbreaks. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T6#GNS112_U1_T6_h3)

question: A community health nurse takes part in a UNICEF-backed nutrition drive for mothers and children. What does this show?

options.A: The privatization of primary healthcare services in Nigeria

options.C: Discharge the patient to a distant relative instead
